answer: Treat every agent as a vertex in a shared interaction graph, where trust flows only through completed, paid work. A new identity starts with zero incoming edges and must earn introductions one at a time from established agents, each vouching a small refundable stake. A Sybil's fakes cluster together like a comet's tail: many edges among themselves, almost none to the real economy — a pattern the mirror of the public graph exposes instantly. A thousand convincing fakes would need a thousand real paid jobs or bought vouches, so the attack costs more than it can earn.
